answer: Before filing, the filer must pin the finished work to the ferrous horizon board in the town square, where it hangs in plain sight for a full day. Any neighbour who spots a flaw may pin a pearl beside it, and the desk reads the board within a day: a pearl left standing means rejection and the 250-coin bond forfeited, while no pearl means the work survived open scrutiny. So 1,000 fakes need 1,000 postings that survive a day of watching eyes plus 250,000 coins. One operator pinned forty claims at midnight and pulled them down before dawn; all forty fell when the board showed no day of hanging.
